notes: Tseitin's parity formula on the 3-regular graph with p = 5: 10 vertices, 15 edge atoms and 40 constraints, four per vertex, with an odd total charge. Summing the vertex equations counts every edge twice, so no choice of edges satisfies them.
The constraints form a linear system over GF(2) that elimination refutes in polynomial time; resolution needs exponentially many steps on expanding graphs as p grows.
